column2: Grand Crusader

Twice now [Root.GetTitledFirstName] has ridden at the head of a Great Crusade, and twice the banners of the faith have followed [Root.GetHerHim] to victory. Across all the lands of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] faiths [Root.GetSheHe] is hailed as the most fearless of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faithful, and peasants press forward to touch the hem of [Root.GetHerHis] cloak as [Root.GetSheHe] passes.\n\nThe minstrels already sing of the [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] line as the sword of the gods. Whatever crusades are called in the years to come, the children of this house will be expected to ride in the van.
Where the gods lead, I follow.
Commander of the Crusade

Forward! I roar, cutting down another man who charges me. "For [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]! To victory!"

The press of the battle carries my guards away, and I set my teeth for what comes next. Through the dust I can see their commander, sitting his horse well behind the line with a grin on his face. If I fall today, he falls with me. Cut follows cut, and his grin fades to a grimace as the fight he thought was far away drags him in.

When the battle settles, I stand over him and what is left of his retinue. "My [Root.GetLordLady], are you hurt?" one of my guards gasps, staring at the blood on me. Little of it is mine.
Hurt? I have never felt better.
The Errantry War

[From.GetTitledName] has declared an Errantry War against the Sultans of Araby. The knights of Antoch have long kept their watch on the edge of the sands, and now they mean to carry the Lady's banner into the desert itself, as the knights of Bretonnia did when the Arabyans first dared to land in Estalia.

Every Knight Errant who rides south and lives may come home a Knight of the Realm, and the young lords of Bretonnia are already sharpening their lances. In the desert cities the sorcerers of the Sultans are said to be calling up winds and djinn to meet them.

It will be years before the host is ready to sail. When it does, the sand will drink a great deal of blood.
For the Lady and the King!
Perhaps I could ask the §Y[d_knights_of_antoch.GetName]§! to march on my Arabyan neighbours?
The Bretonnians and their endless questing.
Let them bleed each other in the sand.
Let them come. The desert is a grave for armies.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName]

[northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName] is a danger to every faithful soul in the south, and I agree that [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetSheHe] must be dealt with. My knights are ready to ride for the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands. I ask nothing of you but your prayers, and that you keep vigil for us in the chapel of the Lady.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
Ride, and may the Lady guard you.
Wait. I must think on this.

[Root.GetTitledName]

My knights are ready to march against [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName], but horses, ships and men-at-arms do not come cheap, and the desert eats all three. If you want this war, you must help pay for it.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
Take the gold, and ride.
Wait. I must think on this.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I agree that [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName] is a dangerous foe, but my order cannot wage war on the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands from across the sea. Give us a foothold close to the enemy, a castle and the land around it, and my knights will do the rest.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
The land is yours. Ride.
Give §Y[From.GetTitledName]§! all the land of your realm in §Y[northern_crusade_duchy_title.GetFullBaseName]§!
Wait. I must think on this.
The Knights Sail South

The host of Antoch has sailed for the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands, a forest of lances and pennants on the decks, the Grail embroidered on every sail. The knights sing hymns to the Lady as they go, and the Knights Errant among them talk of nothing but the glory waiting in the sand.

Their first quarry is [northern_crusade_target_character.GetTitledFirstName], lord of [northern_crusade_target_character.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName]. If [northern_crusade_target_character.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName] falls, the order means to make it a fortress from which to bring the rest of the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands to heel.

No quarter has been promised to the servants of the Sultans.
For the Lady and the King!
The Bretonnians and their endless questing.
And so the knights ride into the sand...

To the esteemed [Root.GetTitledName]

The Knights of Antoch thank you for your aid in the war for [northern_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. Your name will be read out in our chapel at every vigil.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the esteemed [Root.GetTitledName]

The Knights of Antoch thank you for your aid in the war for [northern_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. Your name will be read out in our chapel at every vigil, and we send with this letter a share of the spoils of the desert, as is only right.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
It was the least I could do.
The Errantry War Fails

Twice the Knights of Antoch have ridden into the desert, and twice the sand has thrown them back. Thirst, sickness and the sorcery of the Sultans have done what no Arabyan lance could, and [From.GetTitledName] has called the Errantry War to an end.

The knights limp home with empty saddles behind them, and the Knights Errant who rode south hoping for glory have found graves instead. In the courts of Araby the Sultans are already talking of the north, and of how soft the faithful of the Lady have grown.

Bretonnia's southern shore may soon see dhows full of raiders.
How could the Lady abandon us?
Another failure for the [From.Religion.GetName] faithful.
Neither side deserved to win.
The desert has spoken!
Friend of Antoch

A great honour guard of the Knights of Antoch has ridden up to the gates of [Root.Capital.GetName], with [From.GetTitledName] [From.GetHerselfHimself] at their head. In thanks for my aid in their wars against Araby, the order has named me and all my blood the friends of Antoch, and [From.GetTitledName] presents me with a knight's helm bearing the order's crest.\n\nFor as long as my line endures, the order will ride at our side should we ever have need of them.
It is an honour.
[northern_crusade_kingdom.GetBaseName] Is Won

It has been a long and bitter war between the Knights of Antoch and the people of the [northern_crusade_kingdom.GetAdjective] lands, but the Errantry War has at last ended in victory for the Lady.

The chapels of the Grail now stand where the domes of Araby once rose, and the knights of the order ride the desert roads to keep them safe for the faithful. A score of Knights Errant have come home as Knights of the Realm, and the minstrels have a new war to sing about.

The Sultans of Araby will not soon forget it.
For the Lady and the King!
Well fought, I suppose.
Bretonnia grows bold.
The sand will take it back, in time.
Errantry War for [Title.GetBaseName]
$ORDER$ Errantry War for $OTHER_TITLE$
Holy Order War for [Title.GetBaseName]
$ORDER$ Holy Order War for $OTHER_TITLE$
Errantry War Won
§Y[d_knights_of_antoch.Holder.GetTitledName]§! has §G10§! or higher opinion of §Y[This.GetTitledName]§!
Antochian Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
For [Root.GetHerHis] aid to the Knights of Antoch in their wars against Araby, [Root.GetHerHis] line is held a sworn friend of the order.
Helm of Antoch
Every §YKnight Errant§! who rode in the Errantry War becomes a §YKnight of the Realm§!
A knight's helm crested with the Grail and the arms of the Knights of Antoch, given only to the order's truest friends.

The fleet rides at anchor off [diverted_creditor.Capital.GetName]: galleys, cogs and horse-ships enough to carry the whole Errantry War to the sands of Araby. [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] built every hull of it on the order's word, and now the reckoning has come. The coffers of the order hold not a tenth of the price.\n\nThe Tilean does not shout. A map is unrolled across the table instead. "[diverted_port.GetName] lies on your road south, my lord. Its walls are old, its granaries are full, and its master, [diverted_target.GetTitledName], has cost me more than ships ever will. Take it for me, keep the plunder, and we shall call the debt paid. The Lady need never know."
[diverted_port.GetName] it is. The Lady forgives a debt honourably paid.
Empty the coffers. We pay in gold, not in Old World blood.
A knight of the Grail owes nothing to a merchant. Let him whistle for his coin.
The Errantry Turns

Word runs along the coasts of Tilea faster than any galley. The fleet built to carry [From.GetTitledName] and the Knights of Antoch to Araby has not sailed south. It has turned for [diverted_port.GetName], and the knights mean to storm it at the bidding of [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName], who built their ships and was never paid for them.\n\nIn the temples of Myrmidia the priests are bricking up the treasuries, and [diverted_target.GetTitledName] is calling every sellsword in Tilea to the walls.
Treachery! Every sellsword in Tilea, to the walls!
A debt is a debt, and now it will be paid in [diverted_target.GetFirstName]'s gold.
The Lady weeps to see her knights turned hired swords.
So much for the honour of Bretonnia.
The Sack of [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName]

[diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] has fallen. For three days the knights of the Errantry War and the sellswords of [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] went through the city street by street. They stripped the gold from the altars of Myrmidia, dragged the strongboxes of the merchant princes down to the quays and burned whatever they could not carry. Those who fought were cut down in the canals and piazzas, and those who did not were robbed all the same.\n\nWhat is left of the city now belongs to [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName]. The knights have the gold, and the fleet sails on for Araby with blood on its banners.
The Lady's work needs gold. Let none ask how it was got.
The debt is paid, and [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] is mine.
They will pay for this, every knight of them.
Knights of the Grail, sacking Old World cities like Norscan reavers!
The Errantry War has found easier prey than Araby.
Your house founds the bloodline §YBlood of the Sack§!
The Siege of [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] Is Broken

The knights of the Errantry War have been thrown back from [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName]. Tilean crossbows and pikes held the walls, and the fleet built to carry the knights to Araby now carries their wounded home. [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] has neither the city nor the coin, and the Knights of Antoch have neither the city nor their honour.
The Lady has judged us. We sail for Araby, and pray.
Let every knight of Bretonnia remember [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName].
Sellswords would have done better, and cost less.
Sack [Title.GetBaseName] for the debt of ships
$ORDER$ Sack of $OTHER_TITLE$
Sacked by the Errantry
Knights of the Grail plundered this city to pay for their fleet. Its trade is ruined, its granaries are empty and its people are still clearing the rubble.
Blood of the Sack
The house of the knight who turned the Errantry War on a Tilean port and paid the debt of ships in Old World blood. Its heirs are feared, and they know how to make a prisoner talk.
Sacked an Old World City
§BHoly Fury:§! The Debt of Ships
Once a game, the Tilean prince who built the fleet of the Errantry War may demand his price, and the Knights of Antoch may sack Miragliano, Remas or Luccini to pay it.
The Knights of Antoch always sail straight for Araby.

Two years have passed since I swore to take back the south, and not one blow has been struck. The levies have drifted home to their fields, the ship-owners have found better-paying cargo, and the taverns of my capital have started to joke about my oath.\n\nThe moment has passed.
Another time, perhaps.

[Root.GetTitledName]

When you march to take back the south, my banners will march with yours. Send word, and I will come.

Your ally,
[From.GetTitledName]
A true friend of the south.

[Root.GetTitledName]

The hour has come. My host marches against the occupiers, and I hold you to your promise. Bring your swords.

[From.GetTitledName]
I gave my word. We ride.
The Condottiere

Twice now the lords of the south have marched to take these lands back, and twice I have stood against them, faithful to the gods of the Old World and faithful to whoever paid me. The reconquistadors call me a traitor. The occupiers call me a heathen. Both of them pay me.\n\nIn the taverns from Magritta to Miragliano they sing of me as the finest captain of the age, and they are not wrong. My children will inherit my sword, my name and my price.
Loyalty is expensive. Skill more so.
The Reconqueror

Land by land, I have torn the south back from the hands of those who took it. Where foreign banners flew there are temples of the Old World gods again, and the people line the roads to throw flowers under the hooves of my horse.\n\nThe priests already call me the Reconqueror, and an old helm that is said to have belonged to one of the captains who drove Jaffar's host into the sea was brought out of a temple vault for me. My line will be remembered as long as the south is free.
The south is ours again.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I hear you are at war, and that the war is not going as well as it could. I have men, I have horses, and I am not overly troubled about whose side the gods are on. For a fair price my swords are yours.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Name your price.
I do not hire turncoats.

[Root.GetTitledName]

Your terms are accepted. The gold is on its way. See that your swords earn it.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I would rather lose this war than win it with the help of a sellsword who has no loyalty but to his purse. Keep your swords.

[From.GetTitledName]
Their loss.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I am at war over the south, and I am told your swords can be bought. I will pay well if you fight for me, and I will not ask what your priests think of it.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Gold is gold. I will fight.
Some things are not for sale.

[Root.GetTitledName]

The gold is received. My swords march to join yours.

[From.GetTitledName]
Good.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I am not a sellsword, whatever you may have heard. Find someone else to bleed for you.

[From.GetTitledName]
Pity.

My marshal brings the muster rolls. Every village in the realm can give men for the war, but men without arms, training or pay are little better than a mob.\n\n"How much are we willing to spend, my [Root.GetLordLady]?"
Give them spears and bows.
Arm them properly.
Only the best: pikes, horses, armour.
Not a single crown. Let them bring their pitchforks.

A messenger arrives from [Root.RelHead.GetTitledName]. The temple has heard of my oath to take back the south, and its coffers are open to me, for a price. The priests will want a share of the glory, and a share of my devotion, in return.\n\nOr I could tell them that this war is between me and the gods, and needs no priest's gold.
I will take a little of the temple's gold.
I will take all the temple can give.
The gods' blessing is enough.

A scarred captain presents [new_commander.GetHerselfHimself] at court. [new_commander.GetFirstName] has fought Arabyans in the dunes, greenskins in the Border Princes and pirates off Sartosa, and has heard that I am raising a host to take back the south.\n\n"I have led men into worse places than the ones you are going, my [Root.GetLordLady]. Give me a command and I will show you."
Stay at my court.
Take a command.
I have captains enough.

The land of the occupiers lies across the water as often as over the hills, and an army without ships will march a long way round. The ship-owners of my ports, and a Tilean merchant prince or two, offer to hire out their galleys for the war, at a price.
Hire the galleys.
We will march.

The year of preparation is over. The levies are drilled, the captains chosen, the galleys waiting in harbour. Everyone in the realm knows what comes next.\n\nThe south will be free again, or I will die trying.
To war!
An Oath for the South

[From.GetTitledName] has sworn before the altars of [From.Religion.GetName] to take back the lands of Estalia and Tilea that are held by foreign masters. Long ago the Sultan Jaffar's host landed in Estalia and was flung back into the sea, and [From.GetTitledName] means to do it again, to the Sultans and to every other invader who has taken a foothold in the south.\n\nThe levies are already mustering. In a year, perhaps two, the host will march.
May the gods guide [From.GetHerHis] sword.
Let them come. We will be waiting.
The South Is Free

The last foreign banner in Estalia and Tilea has been torn down. From the Irrana Mountains to the Tilean Sea, every land of the south is held by lords who bow to the gods of the Old World.\n\nThe temples ring their bells, the merchants count the trade that will flow again, and old soldiers tell the young ones about the war. The Reconquest of the South is over.
Praise the gods!
They have won, for now.

A young [From.GetWomanMan] with a fine sword and a finer tongue has come to court. [From.GetSheHeCap] is [From.GetFirstName], an adventurer of [From.Culture.GetName] blood who has sworn to win back the lands of the south from their foreign masters, with or without the help of [From.GetHerHis] betters.\n\n"I ask only your blessing, my [Root.GetLordLady], and whatever else you see fit to give. The men will follow me. The gods will do the rest."
You have my blessing, and more.
I want no part of this.
[FromFrom.GetFirstName] is preparing to march, and my court is waiting to see what kind of patron I will be. My name, my prayers or my purse: any of them would help the young adventurer's cause.
Let [FromFrom.GetHerHim] fight under my banner.
I will pray for [FromFrom.GetHerHis] victory.
Take some gold.
My blessing is enough.
Swear the Reconquest
Swear to take back the lands of Estalia and Tilea from their foreign masters: a year of preparation, then war, land by land. An oath like this is sworn once in a lifetime.
Promise to Join the Reconquest
Promise to join §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! when [Root.GetSheHe] marches to take back the south.
Sell Your Sword to the Occupiers
Offer your swords to §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! against the Reconquest, for gold.

Offer §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! gold to fight for you against the Reconquest.
Sell Your Sword to the Reconquest
Offer your swords to §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! for the Reconquest, for gold.
Hire a Foreign Sellsword
Offer §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! gold to fight for the Reconquest.
No other Reconquest of the South is under way
The Reconquest is still led by the one who swore it
The Reconquest
Condottiere Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
A faithful captain who twice threw back the Reconquest of the South for foreign gold, remembered as the finest sellsword of [Root.GetHerHis] age.
Reconqueror Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
The lord who tore the lands of the south back from their foreign masters.
Reconqueror's Helm
An old helm said to have been worn by one of the captains who threw the Sultan Jaffar's host back into the sea.

Estalian and Tilean lords may swear to take back the south, and adventurers may do it for them.

There is no Reconquest of the South.

My dear [Root.GetTitledName]
The Knights Mariner have long sought a harbour from which to guard the seas in Manann's name and keep [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] ships safe from corsairs and worse. We think your newfound lands in [potential_title.GetBaseName] would make the perfect stronghold, and we would pay you for your troubles.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledName]
Whatever the [d_knights_mariner.GetName] want, I offer.
§Y[potential_title.GetBaseName]§! is given to §Y[From.GetTitledName]§!.
No, I need these lands.
The Knights Mariner of [potential_title.GetBaseName]

The magnanimous [From.GetTitledName] has donated the island of [potential_title.GetBaseName] to the Knights Mariner, the sea-going order of Manann. From their new harbour the knights will hunt the corsairs and raiders that plague the shipping lanes, and [d_knights_mariner.Holder.GetTitledFirstName] vows to keep the waters safe for all faithful sailors of the Old World.
Manann watch over the Knights of [potential_title.GetBaseName].

[Root.GetTitledName]
The White Wolves would finally drive the enemies of Ulric from the north, and your newly won lands of [holy_order_potential_title.GetBaseName] would serve us as a march against the Wastes. We will pay you well for them, for we would not insult a lord of your standing.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledName]
I would be glad to help the [d_knights_of_the_white_wolf.GetName]!
§Y[holy_order_potential_title.GetBaseName]§! is given to §Y[d_knights_of_the_white_wolf.Holder.GetTitledName]§!.
My apologies, but these lands are my own.
The White Wolves in [holy_order_potential_title.GetName]

Supported by the charitable [From.GetTitledName], the Knights of the White Wolf have settled in [holy_order_potential_title.GetBaseName]. Sworn to drive the enemies of the faith from the north, [d_knights_of_the_white_wolf.Holder.GetTitledName] has begun fortifying [holy_order_potential_title.GetName] as a staging ground for the wars to come.\n\nFrom [FromFrom.Capital.GetName], it is only a matter of time before Ulric's knights carry their hammers across the rest of [kingdom_title.GetBaseName]. The northmen look towards the new seat of the White Wolves with fear and hatred.
It is only a matter of time before the north falls to them.

[Root.GetTitledName]
I write to tell you that my brothers and I have left your service. We no longer hold you fit to command the sworn swords of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], and from this day we answer to the god alone.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledName]
Cursed zealots!
Sea-Compass of the Knights Mariner
A brass compass from a harbour of the Knights Mariner, given in thanks to a lord who gave the order a home. Sailors swear its needle swings toward the favour of Manann as surely as toward the north.
Pelt of the White Wolf
A great wolf pelt, like those the Knights of the White Wolf wear over their armour, given in thanks to a lord who helped the order march north. It still smells of pine smoke and snow.
The Knights Mariner send a squadron of §Y20 galleys§! to sail under your banner.
A lance of §Y150 White Wolf knights§! and §Y150 sworn foot§! rides in your service, at half the usual upkeep.

A gift to the order's war chest will be remembered by its Grand Master and by the faithful.
Expel the Order
Drive this order and its knights out of my realm and take back the castles they hold on my land. The faithful will not forgive it easily.
Most righteous [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

column1: I write to you in the matter of your debt to the [holy_order_master.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. Our war against the enemies of [holy_order_master.Religion.GetHighGodName] knows no rest, and we have need of noble warriors to lead our brothers. Your son [holy_order_recruit.GetFirstName] is of an age to take the vows. Send him to us, and we will consider the debt paid in full. He will, of course, renounce his inheritance and any wife he has.
In the service of the faith,

column2: Very well. It is a good life.
I will pay back the gold instead.
Never!
My dear [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

column1: I write to you in the matter of your debt to the [holy_order_master.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. The order needs more castles to train its brothers and keep its war chest full, and there is a fine site for one in [holy_order_castle_site.GetName]. Grant us leave to build there, at our own cost, and we will consider the debt paid in full.
In the service of the faith,

column2: A reasonable request.
The brothers of the [holy_order_master.PrimaryTitle.GetName] have raised a castle in [Root.GetName]. The order's banner flies from its gatehouse.
Impressive!
Most righteous [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

column1: The [holy_order_master.PrimaryTitle.GetName] needs more castles to train its brothers and guard the faithful, and there is a fine site for one in your demesne, in [holy_order_castle_site.GetName]. I offer you 100 gold for the right to build a chapter castle there, at the order's own cost. Its knights would ride against any enemy of [holy_order_master.Religion.GetHighGodName] who threatens your lands.
In the service of the faith,

column2: Build it, with my blessing.
Not on my land.

A column of armoured riders comes up the road beneath the banner of the [holy_order_master.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. Their commander kneels before me. The Grand Master has not forgotten who gave the order its castle, he says, and has sent a lance of his best knights and their men-at-arms to ride under my banner for as long as I live.
Welcome, brothers. You honour my house.
